record.original_question: What is the complexity of the problem of determin- ing whether a regular F -factorization possesses synchronization property, when the parameters of the synchronization are not given? What about this problem for context-freeF -factorizations?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of the problem of determin- ing whether a regular F -factorization possesses synchronization property, when the parameters of the synchronization are not given? What about this problem for context-freeF -factorizations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a finite set of words over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$. An $F$-factorization of a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is a decomposition $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_n$ with each $u_i \in F$. A language $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$ is called an $F$-factorization language if every word of $L$ admits an $F$-factorization (where the factors used are recorded by the derivation/recognition device).

Say that an $F$-factorization language $L$ has the synchronization property with parameters $(k, m)$ (where $k, m$ are positive integers) if for every $w \in L$ and every two $F$-factorizations $w = u_1 \cdots u_n = v_1 \cdots v_{n'}$, whenever a prefix $u_1 \cdots u_i$ and a prefix $v_1 \cdots v_j$ have lengths differing by at most $m$, the suffixes of factorizations agree after at most $k$ further factors. (Equivalently, after any local discrepancy of size at most $m$ between two factorizations, the two factorizations re-synchronize within $k$ blocks.)

We say $L$ has the synchronization property (without specified parameters) if there exist some $k, m \geq 1$ such that $L$ has the synchronization property with parameters $(k, m)$.

Determine the computational complexity of each of the following decision problems:

(1) Given a regular $F$-factorization language $L$ (specified by a finite automaton together with the finite set $F$), decide whether $L$ has the synchronization property (with the parameters $k, m$ not given as part of the input, i.e., quantified existentially).

(2) The same problem when $L$ is presented as a context-free $F$-factorization language (specified by a context-free grammar together with $F$).
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on synchronization properties of F-factorizations and on the complexity of related synchronization problems for regular and context-free languages return work on adjacent topics (synchronizing words under regular constraints, synchronized context-free languages, factorization of synchronous CFGs) but no source that resolves the specific complexity question for the synchronization property of regular or context-free F-factorizations with unspecified parameters. No direct evidence of a solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Computational Complexity of Synchronization Under Sparse Regular Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the constrained synchronization problem for regular constraint languages, but not the F-factorization synchronization property.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent work on synchronization under regular constraints; does not resolve the F-factorization version.

status_evidence.title: On the Computational Complexity of Synchronized Context-Free Languages
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes complexity for membership and emptiness for synchronized context-free languages, a different notion from F-factorization synchronization.
status_evidence.claim: Related complexity results for synchronized CFLs do not address the stated question.
